mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity supports risk asset demand.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 3.0% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 5.0% over 3 months indicates tightening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE declines below 5.0% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 120.0 indicates sustained manufacturing expansion that correlates with rising corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 120.0.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 11000.0 billion dollars signals expanding economic activity that increases corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 exceeds 11000.0.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 195.0 triggers expectations of monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 195.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market strength that fuels consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS above 4.0% during monetary tightening cycles increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.
